business_summary.text: The Company is the largest single coal producing company in India in terms of production in Fiscal 2026, accounting for 21.0% of domestic coal production (source: CRISIL Report).
Its primary product is non-coking coal, including washed/beneficiated coal, sold to power utilities, captive power plants, IPPs and non-power industries such as cement and sponge iron.
Coal production increased 5.92% from 206.10 million tonnes in Fiscal 2024 to 218.31 million tonnes in Fiscal 2026.

The Company operates 17 mines (14 opencast and 3 underground) in the Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields, Odisha, plus one 10 MTPA coal washery at Lakhanpur; opencast mines contributed 99.85% of production in Fiscal 2026.
Long-term Fuel Supply Agreements accounted for 82.12% of revenue from sale of products in Fiscal 2026, and its customer base spans 16 states in India.

concentration.text: Top 10 customers contributed 55.94% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026 (₹170,888.47 million) and 51.95% in the six months ended September 30, 2026.
Top customer contributed 14.64% (₹44,719.00 million) and top 5 customers 41.09% (₹125,528.58 million) of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026.
Sales to the thermal power sector (State, Central GENCO and IPPs) were 68.62% of sale of products in Fiscal 2026 and 69.64% in the six months ended September 30, 2026.

Revenue from government-owned and controlled power generation companies and utilities was 44.81% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026 (₹136,900.36 million) and 41.68% in the six months ended September 30, 2026.
Raw non-coking coal accounted for 97.41% of sale of products in Fiscal 2026 and 97.38% in the six months ended September 30, 2026.
Top 10 contractors accounted for 63.61% of contractual expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2026 and 60.02% in Fiscal 2026.
Five of the top 10 customers for the six months ended September 30, 2026 have coastal thermal plants that can switch to imported coal.

industry.text: Thermal power accounted for approximately 70% of India's electricity generation in Fiscal 2026 (source: CRISIL Report).

Demand for non-coking coal in India increased from 1,112 million tonnes in Fiscal 2025 to 1,186 million tonnes in Fiscal 2026, with a projected demand of 1,564 million tonnes in Fiscal 2036 (source: CRISIL Report).
Coal demand from power plants stood at 698 million tonnes in Fiscal 2025 and is expected to reach 843 million tonnes by Fiscal 2031 (source: CRISIL Report).
Power-sector demand for non-coking coal is projected to decline from 934.40 million tonnes in Fiscal 2035 to 927.80 million tonnes in Fiscal 2038 as renewable energy emerges (source: CRISIL Report).
Coal India Limited produced 768.19 MT in Fiscal 2026 and accounted for 73.8% of domestic coal production; the Company accounted for 28.4% of Coal India Limited's production (source: CRISIL Report).
Domestic coal output reached 1.05 billion tonnes in Fiscal 2025.

promoters.name: President of India, acting through the Ministry of Coal, Government of India
promoters.background: Individual Promoter; holds Nil pre-Offer equity shares directly; is the promoter of Coal India Limited.

promoters.name: Coal India Limited
promoters.background: Corporate Promoter holding 6,618,363,000 equity shares (100.00%) pre-Offer; a listed 'Maharatna' central public sector enterprise engaged in production and marketing of coal, incorporated June 14, 1973 as Coal Mines Authority Limited; the President of India holds 61.13% of it.

strengths.text: Largest single coal producing company in India with 21.00% of domestic coal production in Fiscal 2026 and JORC audited reserves of 9,840.31 MT, enough for around 45 years at current production.
Allocated blocks hold an estimated coal resource of approximately 40.34 billion tonnes under ISP Guidelines, 9.80% of India's total coal resource as at April 1, 2026.
Strategic support and resources of Coal India Limited, the largest coal producing company in the world, including R&D and exploration support from CMPDIL.
Low-cost mechanised mining: surface miners accounted for 99.37% of production in Fiscal 2026, and the Company had the lowest production cost per tonne among Coal India Limited's subsidiaries.
Output per manshift of 30.34 tonnes in Fiscal 2026, 2.4 times that of Coal India Limited on a consolidated basis.
Rail-led evacuation network: railways accounted for 65.28% of total coal dispatch in Fiscal 2026, up from 58.70% in Fiscal 2024, with access to five ports.

risks.title: Dependence on raw non-coking coal
risks.detail: Raw non-coking coal accounted for 97.41% of sale of products in Fiscal 2026. CRISIL says demand may decline after Fiscal 2036, and under a net zero pathway coal demand falls to about 161 million tonnes by 2070.

risks.title: Dependence on the thermal power sector
risks.detail: Thermal power sales were 68.62% of sale of products in Fiscal 2026. Power-sector sales fell 4.82% to ₹204,854.09 million in Fiscal 2026, mainly because renewables contributed more to the grid.

risks.title: Government customers and delayed receivables
risks.detail: Government-owned power utilities contributed 44.81% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026. Payments are delayed from Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation (₹19,298.80 million) and Andhra Pradesh Power Development Company (₹5,021.60 million) as at September 30, 2026.

risks.title: Large contingent liabilities
risks.detail: Total contingent liabilities of ₹125,132.90 million were 55.86% of Net Worth as at September 30, 2026, and they are not provided for in the financial statements.

risks.title: Dependence on Coal India Limited and conflicts of interest
risks.detail: The Company is wholly owned by Coal India Limited, its executive employees are seconded from Coal India Limited on terms that can be changed, and sister subsidiaries in coal mining may create conflicts of interest.

risks.title: Customer concentration and captive blocks or imports
risks.detail: Top 10 customers were 55.94% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026. Customers may cut offtake if they win captive or commercial coal blocks or switch to imported coal.

risks.title: Reliance on third-party contractors
risks.detail: Contractual expenses were ₹68,236.20 million (22.34% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026, and the top 10 contractors made up 63.61% of contractual expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2026.

risks.title: Hazardous operations and inadequate insurance
risks.detail: There were 13 fatal accident cases between April 1, 2023 and September 30, 2026. The Company does not maintain insurance coverage in line with applicable industry standards.

litigation.category: Criminal proceedings by the Company – complaints before SDJM Talcher and Jharsuguda over obstruction and trespass at mines
Criminal proceedings by the Company – complaints under section 630 of the Companies Act, 1956 to vacate employee quarters
Criminal – maintenance petitions where the Company is a proforma party
Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal cases against the Company
Material civil – the Company's challenge to the State of Odisha's 15% tax on coal-bearing lands under the ORISED Act, pending before the Supreme Court

contingent_liabilities.text: Total contingent liabilities were ₹125,132.90 million as at September 30, 2026, 55.86% of Net Worth of ₹223,998.03 million.
Income tax contingent liabilities were ₹80,748.30 million as at September 30, 2026, against ₹49,957.40 million as at March 31, 2026.
Water tax contingent liabilities were ₹8,573.80 million and royalty ₹2,250.80 million as at September 30, 2026.
Miscellaneous land compensation and other contingent liabilities were ₹21,010.00 million as at September 30, 2026.

Demand notices of ₹28,640.70 million alleging production above Environmental Clearance limits are not counted as contingent liabilities, because the Company considers an outflow remote after a Revisional Authority set aside similar orders.

related_party.text: The net amount receivable from Coal India Limited was ₹562.50 million (0.35% of revenue from operations) for the six months ended September 30, 2026; the net amount payable was ₹432.80 million in Fiscal 2026.
Executive employees are seconded from Coal India Limited; the Company pays their salaries and Coal India Limited does not reimburse them.
CMPDIL, a Coal India Limited subsidiary and promoter group company, provides exploration, mine planning and R&D services under an annual work programme paid through arm's-length contracts.
None of the top 10 customers are related parties.

red_flags.text: Receivables are delayed from Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation Limited (₹19,298.80 million) and Andhra Pradesh Power Development Company Limited (₹5,021.60 million) as at September 30, 2026.
Contingent liabilities rose to ₹125,132.90 million (55.86% of Net Worth) as at September 30, 2026 from ₹85,062.30 million as at March 31, 2026.
The Company does not maintain insurance coverage in accordance with applicable industry standards.
There were 13 fatal accident cases between April 1, 2023 and September 30, 2026.
Research and development expense was nil in Fiscals 2026 and 2025 and ₹0.50 million in Fiscal 2024.
The Company's Chief Medical Officer was convicted under the PCPNDT Act, the conviction was upheld on appeal, and a revision petition is pending before the Orissa High Court.
Industry data comes from the CRISIL Report, which the Company exclusively commissioned and paid for.

notes: The segment split shown is by product for Fiscal 2026. The RHP also splits sale of products by industry for the same year (Power generation 68.62%, Captive power plants 16.57%, Others 14.81%, page 233); it is left out to avoid duplication.
Only pages 24-33 of Risk Factors were provided, so risks after risk factor 9 are not covered.
The Industry Overview pages provided (146-149) cover mainly the macroeconomy; the coal industry figures above come from Risk Factors and Our Business.
The Outstanding Litigation pages are incomplete: tax claims, regulatory actions, director and promoter litigation and the rest of the material civil proceedings are not on the pages provided.
No full related-party transactions note and no auditor's report or emphasis of matter are on these pages.
